subject: Dedicated capacity SLI carveout & queueing runbook — AtlasGrid
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@atlasgrid.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: emily.ramos@atlasgrid.com, procurement@atlasgrid.com
Date: Tue, 1 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity SLI/queueing ask and runbook request

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. AtlasGrid is preparing our production rollout and we have one outstanding concern before we can sign: our nightly ingestion jobs (01:00–04:00 PT) need a temporary increase in sustained throughput that will overlap with low-volume online traffic. We run model scoring + embedding generation off a 16-GPU reserved pool.

Two concrete asks:
1) A temporary carveout (3-hour window) for higher sustained throughput for batch windows without degrading our p95 tail for interactive traffic beyond 120ms.
2) A queueing/runbook addendum that specifies how Redwood will ration burst tokens, preemption behavior, and KV cache affinity during the window — we need predictable degraded behavior rather than opaque failures.

I've attached a rough SLO draft with our expected token counts and a proposed fallback schedule. Can Redwood produce a one-page runbook and propose contract language for a short-term SLI credit mechanism if tails slip beyond the threshold?

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform Operations
AtlasGrid Systems

Attachments: atlasgrid-slo-draft-20250401.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@atlasgrid.com>, Emily Ramos <emily.ramos@atlasgrid.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Apr 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLI/queueing ask and runbook request

Sanjay —

Really appreciate the thorough SLO draft; that made this easy to triage. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a controlled carveout but we want to formalize the behavior so your app sees deterministic degradations (graceful tail increase, not hard failures).

Operational proposal (summary):
- Carveout window: 01:00–04:00 PT daily (pilot for first 30 days).
- Burst budget: allow up to +25% throughput over baseline reserved pool for a 3-hour window, implemented as a burst token bank (tokens consumed per token-gen).
- Priority lanes: interactive requests keep a high-priority lane; batch requests get a soft-preemptible lane with a backoff threshold at 75% token burn rate.
- Latency SLI: p95 target 120ms for interactive; if p95 > 150ms for two consecutive 1-hour slices we trigger SLI credits per the attached credit table.
- KV cache affinity: keep sticky KV shard ownership for interactive sessions; batch jobs use ephemeral cache with a warmup allowance to limit cache thrashing.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Karthik and I will draft a concise runbook (1–2 pages) describing the fallback flow + observability hooks (traces, p95 alarms, token-meter).
2) We’ll produce contract wording for a 30-day pilot SLI credit mechanism and a DocuSign-ready addendum.

I’ll loop in Lauren (contracts) on the wording. Any constraints from your procurement side we should be aware of?

Thanks — sending a short runbook draft by EOD tomorrow.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Apr 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity SLI/queueing ask and runbook request

Looping you in for contracts review / quick pricing check. Key points for legal/procurement:
- This is a time-boxed pilot (30 days) with a measurable SLI credit schedule if p95 crosses 150ms during the carveout window.
- We propose the credit as a proportional monthly credit tied to the percent of windows impacted (see sample table in the runbook draft).
- No long-term capacity increase required; we plan to use the existing reserved 16-GPU pool and manage with burst tokens and queue shaping.

Lauren — can you please prepare a one-page addendum (term: 30 days, auto-expire unless both parties opt-in) and a short clause for the MSA that references the runbook ID and the token accounting method? Procurement will want sample language they can send to their legal team.

Also copying a pricing calc below for quick visibility: assumed baseline throughput 1.2M tokens/hour; batch needs up to 3.0M tokens/hour during the window; expected additional cost if burst not covered ~ $X (we'll fill with final numbers before signature).

-Karthik
Director, Customer Solutions
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@atlasgrid.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 17:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLI/queueing ask and runbook request

Sanjay —

Thanks for the details. Attached is a first-pass runbook and a draft addendum (redwood-runbook-draft.odt). Highlights:
- Term: 30-day pilot starting on first production day after signature.
- Credit mechanics: sliding credit based on % of impacted carveout windows (table included).
- Escalation: automated alerts to your operations on p95 breach; 30-min mitigation window before credits apply (gives us time to kick fallback policies).
- Preemption behavior spelled out: we will shift batch jobs to controlled backlog with a soft-preempt threshold to preserve interactive lanes.

If AtlasGrid is comfortable, I can generate a DocuSign envelope with the addendum and the pilot start date field left blank for you to populate. Jonas — please add final pricing numbers to the envelope before I send.

Sanjay — can you confirm procurement contact and whether you want this daily or limited to Mon–Fri? Also confirm who should receive the DocuSign envelope.

Lauren Bishop
Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
